clue.text: Leads away sailor with pipes

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
ducts are pipes or channels carrying air or fluid

explanation.surface: A seaman marches off carrying his bagpipes.
explanation.definitionFit: To abduct is to carry someone off unlawfully, taking them away by force.

clue.text: Charts for finding sea-salt?

indicators.note: the letters of the fodder are to be searched and rearranged, so finding the answer inside them means a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A navigator wonders which maps show where salt can be harvested from the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for finding' signals that the seven letters of SEA-SALT, reshuffled, give the charts.
explanation.definitionFit: Books of maps are bound collections of charts.

clue.text: Like a Lee-Enfield? Yes and no

definitions.text: Like a Lee-Enfield? Yes and no

parts.words: Like a Lee-Enfield? Yes and no
parts.note: the Lee-Enfield is a single-barrel British army rifle, so as a gun it is not two-barrelled, yet its hyphenated name is

explanation.surface: A quiz about whether an old service rifle fits a description gets an equivocal reply.
explanation.walkthrough: The term describes both a two-barrelled shotgun and a hyphenated surname; the Lee-Enfield rifle has one barrel but a hyphenated name, hence 'Yes and no'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hyphenated name such as Lee-Enfield is called double-barrelled by analogy with a twin-barrel gun.

clue.text: Escaroles in this stew?

indicators.note: a stew mixes its ingredients, so the letters of the salad leaves are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether bitter salad leaves belong in the pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew' is both the anagram signal on ESCAROLES and the description of the dish, so the whole clue defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a slow-cooked dish of meat or vegetables in liquid, i.e. a stew, and escarole could go in one.

clue.text: Several thousand held within WW 1 battle area

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside another, so the letter for thousand sits within the word for several

parts.note: some means several, an unspecified number
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Thousands of soldiers were trapped in a First World War battle zone.
explanation.definitionFit: The river in northern France gave its name to a major 1916 battle and its battlefield.

clue.text: Material of knitted ties, presented to cricketer

parts.note: a bat is a batsman, a cricketer who bats

indicators.note: knitting works strands into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fabric from some knitted neckwear is given as a gift to a cricket player.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knitted' looks like it describes the neckwear, but it is the anagram signal; 'presented to' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine light cotton or linen fabric, so a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Gas principle of young man, as well turned-out

parts.note: a boy is a young male

indicators.note: turned out suggests the letters are tipped out and set in a new order

explanation.surface: A rule of conduct belonging to a lad who is also smartly dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' reads as idle talk from a young man, but it points to the physics of gases; 'turned-out' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This law of physics says that a gas's pressure varies inversely with its volume at constant temperature.

clue.text: What's-his-name, say, the revolt leader?

parts.note: 'What's' said quickly is Wat, the first name of the man who led the Peasants' Revolt of 1381, so the clue asks for Wat's surname

explanation.surface: Someone struggles to recall the name of the rebel chief.
explanation.walkthrough: Wat led the English Peasants' Revolt of 1381; 'What's-his-name, say' gives 'Wat's his name', and the question is that surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Wat of that surname led the 1381 English peasants' uprising.

clue.text: Union members coerced in these assemblies?

definitions.text: Union members coerced in these assemblies?

parts.words: Union members coerced in these assemblies?
parts.note: reads like strong-arm trade union meetings, but the union is marriage and the members are a couple forced to marry, traditionally because of a pregnancy

explanation.surface: Trade unionists are bullied at their meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' is marriage, not a trade union: these ceremonies are forced on the couple, the bride's father notionally holding a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced marriage, usually because the bride is pregnant, is named after a father with a gun.

clue.text: Call English openers to take championship

indicators.note: only the opening letters of the word are kept, the rest being dropped

parts.note: a title is a championship won in sport

explanation.surface: An announcer invites England's opening batsmen to go out and win the trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English openers' keeps the first two letters, EN, of English; in the surface they are England's opening batsmen in cricket. 'to take' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle a book or person is to name or call it something.

clue.text: Her diminutive females automatically so upset?

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether small women are easily put out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges the fifteen letters of AUTOMATICALLY SO. The definition means 'her Little Women', naming the author through her best-known novel.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist wrote Little Women, so its small women are hers.

clue.text: Crack number in exclusive setting

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another, as a stone goes in a ring
a setting surrounds and holds a jewel, so the word for exclusive encloses the numeral

parts.note: sole means exclusive, as in sole rights
V is the Roman numeral five, a number

explanation.surface: A safecracker works out the combination in a private room.
explanation.definitionFit: To crack a puzzle or code is to work it out.

clue.text: See first at Bath, having girth adjusted? it's a plant!

parts.note: to eye is to look at or see

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is taken
adjusting the strap rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: A rider at Bath notices the saddle girth needs tightening, then spots a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is a verb in the surface but gives a synonym here; Bath is the English spa city, and 'adjusted' signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small meadow flower once used to treat eye complaints.

clue.text: Slow! Vehicle reversing in front of common

indicators.note: the first piece is placed before the second
the vehicle's word is read backwards, like a vehicle backing up

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
normal means common, ordinary

explanation.surface: A warning to a driver backing a vehicle out ahead of the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversing' turns BUS into SUB.
explanation.definitionFit: Below average in intelligence is an old, now offensive sense of 'slow'.

clue.text: Clear leaders in economy, perhaps, with this vehicle

indicators.note: perhaps hints at a possible variant, so the letters are rearranged
only the leading letters of the word are kept, the rest dropped

explanation.surface: Someone praises a single-wheeled ride for leading the way in saving fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clear leaders' keeps CL, the first two letters of Clear; with ECONOMY, 'perhaps' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: A unicycle, with one wheel, is a vehicle for one rider.

clue.text: Kind of art-work in Copenhagen recently

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A style of painting has lately appeared in the Danish capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is inside 'CopenhaGEN REcently'.
explanation.definitionFit: Genre painting is a kind of art showing scenes of everyday life.

clue.text: Reg nicely improved with the syrupy stuff

indicators.note: improving something changes it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Reg's health picks up nicely after a dose of thick medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: This colourless sweet viscous liquid is a syrup-like substance.

clue.text: Air of gravity in dreadful surroundings

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another
the word for dreadful surrounds the gravity symbol

parts.note: dire means dreadful
g is the symbol for acceleration due to gravity

explanation.surface: A solemn tune is played in grim surroundings.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a mournful song for a funeral, an air being a tune.

clue.text: A striking bar-counter, we hear, in the jazz club

definitions.text: A striking bar-counter, we hear, in the jazz club

parts.words: A striking bar-counter, we hear, in the jazz club
parts.note: suggests an impressive bartender, but the musician strikes the skins and counts the bars of music, and is very audible on the club's bandstand

explanation.surface: A remarkable barman serves at a jazz club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' means hitting, and the 'bar' is a measure of music, not a pub counter.
explanation.definitionFit: The percussionist in a band beats time and keeps count of the measures.

clue.text: Pairs off after 7?

parts.note: 7 refers to the clue at 7 down, the forced marriage ceremonies; the couples who leave them have just been married

explanation.surface: A dance caller pairs off the dancers after seven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is a cross-reference to the answer at 7 down, not a time.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples just married leave the ceremony as husband and wife.

clue.text: One who takes coat from Lincoln, for example

definitions.text: One who takes coat from Lincoln, for example

parts.words: One who takes coat from Lincoln, for example
parts.note: suggests a cloakroom attendant serving President Lincoln, but Lincoln is a breed of long-wooled English sheep and its coat is its fleece

explanation.surface: An attendant helps Abraham Lincoln off with his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: The Lincoln is an English breed of sheep with long wool.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheep's fleece is clipped off by a person who cuts wool.

clue.text: Alice Hunt drunk, under the table

indicators.note: being drunk disorders a person, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: Alice Hunt has had so much that she has slid under the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under the table' suggests drunkenness, which belongs to the surface; here it means secret and shady.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal done under the table is dishonest, contrary to moral standards.

clue.text: Mount Sinai's mineral in pencils?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside another

parts.note: HB is the standard grade marked on pencils
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the Biblical mountain's rock is used to make pencil leads.
explanation.walkthrough: HB, 'hard black', is the grade of an ordinary pencil.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, this is another name for the mountain where Moses received the law.

clue.text: Scottish landowner died at place of seclusion

parts.note: a lair is a hidden den or retreat
D is the abbreviation for died, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A Highland estate owner passed away in his secluded retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland the owner of a landed estate holds this title.

clue.text: How poet might supply last university with Head of English

parts.note: the end is the last part

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A verse writer explains how to fund the final college with an English department head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How poet might' marks an old literary word: it means to endow or provide.
explanation.definitionFit: This archaic verb means to endow or provide someone with a quality, a word mostly found in verse.

clue.text: Cowboy ordering premarital tonic

indicators.note: putting things in order sets the letters out afresh

explanation.surface: A ranch hand orders a drink before his wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cowboy' here is the informal sense of an unscrupulous or incompetent tradesman.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense of cowboy is a shoddy or negligent professional, one guilty of professional misconduct.

clue.text: Can take a seat free, then bale out

parts.note: to rid is to free from something

indicators.note: out suggests something is wrong or awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A passenger finds a free seat, then jumps out by parachute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges BALE into ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse or bike that can be ridden is one a person can sit upon and use.

clue.text: Actor's assistant with his back to the wall?

definitions.meaning: a theatre helper who helps performers into their costumes

definitions.text: with his back to the wall?
definitions.meaning: a kitchen sideboard with shelves stands with its back against a wall

explanation.surface: A theatre aide is cornered, desperate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with his back to the wall' sounds like someone in trouble; it describes a piece of furniture standing against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a backstage costume helper and a tall kitchen cupboard with shelves share this name.
